Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: MAP draft: performance benchmarking plan, workload & SLOs

Jordan — attaching the initial MAP section for the performance benchmarking work we discussed on Friday. This email contains the proposed workload definition, measurement plan and candidate success criteria so your team can validate before we run the tests. High level: 

- Scope: 24h synthetic + replayed production traces (sampled) covering 1K typical sessions and edge-case long prompts.
- Metrics: TTFT (first token from request), p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec (throughput), and sustained concurrency behavior.
- Success criteria (proposal): TTFT median <= 150ms; p95 <= 400ms under 150 concurrent sessions; stable throughput >= 12k tokens/sec for sustained 5 minute windows.
- Test variants: baseline model (open-model-v1), quantized (int8) variant, and cached-prefix variant.

Please review the attached scope (acme_map_scope_v1.pdf) and a lightweight workload template (test_workload_template.csv). If these targets look reasonable, we can schedule a 4-hour run next week; Marissa will be the test owner.

Next steps / asks for Acme:
- Confirm the workload sample you want replayed (full traces or anonymized subset).
- Call out any additional SLOs (e.g., p50 TTFT targets for mobile users).
- Preferred windows for test runs (we can do off-peak or a dedicated window).

Thanks — looking forward to locking this into the MAP so it can be part of the demo/close timeline.

--

Date: Sun, 21 Jun 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP draft: performance benchmarking plan, workload & SLOs

Thanks Ava — the proposal looks solid. A few clarifications from our side before you run anything: 

1) Concurrency profile: our peak expected concurrency during business hours is ~200 concurrent interactive sessions for the 2k-user pilot. Can you run a 200-concurrency pass and a 100-concurrency pass? We care most about p95 tail latency at peak.
2) TTFT target: mobile clients are sensitive — can we aim for p50 TTFT <= 120ms as an aspirational goal? If that’s not feasible, at least ensure p95 remains <= 450ms for interactive UX.
3) Workload mix: our traffic is ~70% short prompts (<= 40 tokens), 25% medium (40–250 tokens), 5% long (>250 tokens). Please include this distribution in the replay.

Procurement note: we’d like a preliminary result summary to share with procurement by end of next week (Jun 30) so they can move the contract forward. If the benchmark looks good we’ll target pilot sign-off in the first half of July.

Let me know if you need any additional traces — happy to provide an anonymized sample.

— Jordan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Smith <j.smith@acme-corp.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: MAP draft: performance benchmarking plan, workload & SLOs — initial run results

Folks — ran the first set of passes yesterday (attached results). Quick summary: 

Test configuration (summary):
- Cluster: 4 x A100 equivalent nodes, serving open-model-v1 (fp16) and int8-quant variant.
- Workload: replayed 3k sampled sessions with distribution Jordan specified (70/25/5).
- Concurrency passes: 100 and 200 simultaneous request streams, sustained for 10 minutes per pass.

High level results (see acme_benchmark_results_20260623.csv for full data):
- TTFT (first token): median = 118ms (baseline), p95 = 410ms (baseline) at 150 concurrent sessions (interpolated).
- At 200 concurrency: p95 increased to 680ms for baseline (fp16). Quantized (int8) reduced median by ~10% but tail remained high.
- Throughput: sustained aggregate tokens/sec = 13,200 (baseline) on 150 concurrency; dropped to ~11,000 tokens/sec at 200 concurrency due to queuing/backpressure.
- Observed spikes: long prompt paths (>250 tokens) caused transient KV-cache misses that inflated p99.

Pass/fail vs proposed SLOs: 
- Median TTFT <= 150ms: PASS (118ms)
- p95 <= 400ms @ 150 concurrency: MARGINAL (410ms; slightly above target)
- Stable throughput >= 12k tokens/sec: PASS at 150 concurrency; FAIL at sustained 200 concurrency.

Recommendations to meet MAP targets before pilot:
- Enable prefix/KV caching for repeated session prefixes — we saw ~20–35% tail reduction on cached paths.
- Tune batching window to prefer slightly larger batches during 200-concurrency bursts (adds a few ms median cost but reduces tail significantly).
- Consider a small scale-up to 5 nodes for peak windows (predictable reserved capacity) — that gets p95 down to ~370ms in our re-run.

Attachments included: acme_benchmark_results_20260623.csv, latency_histogram.png (p50/p95/p99 across runs).

I can run the cache-enabled pass and a 5-node re-run tomorrow if you want — that will give a clear pass/fail vs Jordan’s updated p95/p50 asks.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MAP draft: performance benchmarking plan, workload & SLOs — summary & next steps

Jordan — thanks for the quick review and Marissa for the detailed run. Short summary and proposed MAP updates + close timeline: 

What we ran: baseline and quantized passes at 100/150/200 concurrency with your traffic mix (70/25/5). Full results attached in the MAP final PDF.

Key takeaway: baseline median TTFT already meets the proposed median target (118ms < 150ms). p95 at 150 concurrency is marginally above target (410ms vs 400ms). At 200 concurrency we see tail degradation — mitigations below close the gap.

Planned mitigation runs (we will execute immediately if you approve):
- Run A: enable prefix/KV caching + tuned batching (expected p95 improvement ~20–30% on cached flows).
- Run B: 5-node reserved capacity re-run to mirror pilot peak window (expected p95 ~370ms).

Proposed MAP updates (to be included in the shared MAP PDF):
- Acceptance criteria: TTFT median <= 150ms AND p95 <= 400ms at 150-concurrency baseline (pass = green).
- Contingency: if 150-concurrency p95 > 400ms, enable cached-prefix mode as part of pilot sign-off; if 200-concurrency required for your UX, we recommend a small reserved capacity bump.
- Sign-off timeline: preliminary results (this summary + attachments) to procurement by 2026-06-30; pilot contract signature target 2026-07-08; pilot start 2026-07-15.

Next steps / asks:
- Jordan: confirm you want the cache-enabled re-run and whether we should do the 5-node re-run in the same window. If approved, Marissa will run both tomorrow and we’ll update the MAP PDF.
- Procurement: if you can review the preliminary numbers by Jun 30 that helps keep the July cadence.

Thanks — we’ll keep this tight so the MAP can be included in your internal review.
